paper: Longstaff and Schwartz (2001), Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach
verification: Transcribed and visually checked against the original PDF table.
protocol: Eight contracts (S=36 or 44, sigma=.20 or .40, T=1 or 2); five initial seeds each; 100000 in-sample paths and a separate 100000 out-of-sample paths, each with 50000 antithetic pairs; frozen in-sample regression coefficients; K=40, r=.06, 50 exercise dates/year.
printed_precision: Prices, SEs and differences are printed to .001.
known_printed_inconsistency: S=36, sigma=.20, T=2, replicate 3 prints a difference of +.009 although the printed prices 4.820 minus 4.829 give -.009. The CSV preserves the printed sign without silently correcting it.
limitations: Original seeds, RNG and SE formula are unreported. Replicate numbers identify printed rows; they do not identify our new seed values. Compare distributions and aggregate results, not paired original/random-seed rows.
